projects.title: Coursify
projects.description: Website link: https://coursify-ai.vercel.app/A web app that takes in basic information about a course (a course title, and unit titles), generates multiple chapters for each unit and turns it into a full-fledged course with videos, a summary, and a short quiz for each chapter. The app utilizes Google's latest generative AI tool, the Palm 2 API, and the YouTube Search and Transcript APIs to create all the course information.

projects.title: Learndeck - LLM-powered multimedia tutor for iOS and Android

projects.title: Gymify
projects.description: A social, community driven solution to fitness motivation that utilizes flutter, firebase, and the Google Maps API to facilitate the creation of online gym communities in which users can collectively track workouts and easily push their friends to reach their goals. Best Mobile Hack winner at Los Altos Hacks, the biggest high school hackathon in the world.

projects.title: hoophub
projects.description: An app that allows users to easily find and join pickup basketball games in their area. Users can browse a list of games that are starting soon, organize their own games, and join games that are already in progress. The app also allows users to build connections with other hoopers by creating profiles, adding friends, and sending messages.

activity.title: Your vibe-coded app SUCKS. It might work, but it’s filled with nonsense variables, dead code, and loops that are so deeply nested you never reach the body of them. Here’s what’s worrying: 42% of a developer’s week is spent fixing messy code. And LLMs are somehow worse at it than we are; they burn tokens and get nowhere. You know what would save you? Refactorika. Anav Bordia , Jay Thapar , Tanush Aggarwal , and I built the ultimate multi-agent orchestration harness to kill technical debt before it kills you. With just a single command, Refactorika delivers: – Parallel Multi-Agent Orchestration: Concurrent LLM agents diagnosing, isolated patching, and refactoring messy files simultaneously. - Deterministic Atomic Git Patches: Seamless, automated git diff generation with zero-breakage structural state validation. - Vector-Embedded Context Retrieval: Semantic codebase indexing and vector storage that surfaces exactly the right context to agents without bloat. - Model Context Protocol Integration: Unified, real-time context streaming between AI models and local development environments. - Enterprise-Grade Performance: Benchmarked directly against Microsoft’s open-source multi-agent refactoring frameworks, achieving a 40% token reduction, 50% speed increase, and 20% boost in overall accuracy. Also, we won the Cognition track at the Cal Hacks Berkeley AI hackathon! Yay! Check it out here: https://lnkd.in/dQyY9igN

It was a great experience collaborating with Mithil Patil on Coursify. Coursify allows users to create courses on any subject through the power of generative AI. We drew on Khan Academy's course format to include interactive elements like chats and quizzes. For more details, check out Mithil's post.

I had an absolute blast at Viking Hacks a couple weeks back with Anav Bordia Mithil Patil and Soorya Ignatius . After 8 straight hours of problem solving, programming, and getting destroyed in table tennis matches, we managed, at basically the last second, to put out something great. To take away 1st place in the Entertainment track, we made KeyBuddies: a collaborative music production and education platform for kids. With KeyBuddies, users can join or create a studio and work with their peers to make amazing music out of custom or premade loops. Now as a team, we have a good bit of experience at hackathons, but this time, we decided to switch some things up. For once we laid off the energy drinks, our presentation consisted of Soorya Ignatius arranging and me singing “Love Story” by Taylor Swift live in front of the whole crowd, and what I’m personally most proud of — we managed to make something pretty impressive without once using the word “AI”. You already know it’s hackathon season, so stay expecting more updates about our team’s adventures. If you haven’t already, check out our profiles and feel free to drop a follow or slide into our DM’s if you’re interested. As for KeyBuddies, check our some pictures. We've been working on it after the event, so keep your eyes peeled for something big and feel free to drop a comment with your thoughts. Stay safe, stay hungry, and stay coding! I’ll see you guys soon.

Last weekend, Atharv , Mithil , Anav and I had a blast at CruzHacks 2024, a 36-hour hackathon at UC Santa Cruz. To paint you a picture, imagine a hall packed full of pajama-clad CS undergrads hurriedly bodging together caffeine-fueled social justice tools that rely a bit too much on GPT API calls, scattering crushed energy drink cans about and sleeping for mere hours separated from musty old flooring only by stale nylon tarp. If that description sounds chaotic, I've done my job well. But that's why we love hackathons. We've been going to these kinds of events as a team for about a year now, and I think that makes me somewhat qualified to talk about them broadly. Our main takeaway is as follows: nothing beats getting together in person and hammering something out in a hurry. It's like rocket fuel to our growth as coders, designers, presenters, or any of the many other hats we find a good creator must inevitably don. We ended up winning Best Use of Auth0 (cue applause) for our project, Learndeck – a functional mobile app that generates multimedia courses about any topic you could think of, customizing lesson plans to fit your progress, automatically fitting work periods into your busy schedule, drawing from YouTube and academic sources to construct a nuanced and accurate syllabus, and of course, a GPT-powered tutor to answer study-related questions. And while we were angling for first place overall, a win like this against CS and MechEng college students is a win nonetheless. As for our future plans, we're going to keep hitting up hackathons across the state just to see how far we can get. Prize or not, these events are super fun and I can't wait to visit more. That's about all I wanted to share, so I'll leave you with a few photos to wrap things up. Enjoy!

Hey LinkedIn community! We're thrilled to share one of the amazing outcomes of our recent philanthropic hackathon, "Code for Cause." We organized this event with the mission of providing technical support to local organizations. One of our proud collaborations was with BISV DECA! The winning team at our hackathon made an easy-to-use and intuitive app to help streamline BISV DECA's meeting attendance system. After the event, we worked hand-in-hand with the BISV DECA team and the Code for Cause winning team to help the organization get set up and use the app in club operations. Today, we're thrilled to celebrate the successful implementation of the app, making a real difference in optimizing their processes. It's inspiring to see technology catalyze positive change, and we're honored to be part of BISV DECA's journey toward greater efficiency and impact. 🌍💪 A big shoutout to the entire team for their dedication and to BISV DECA for embracing innovation! 🎉 Let's continue making strides together! #CodeForCause #TechForGood #Collaboration #ImpactfulInnovation #BISVDECA

At ArcaLabs this summer, I've been working with sandboxes for our AI agents and developed a neat system for brokering secret-requiring CLIs to protect from prompt injection. Instead of remote execution, I found a way to avoid transferring files over network/scaling an additional API by utilizing Linux primitives for secret isolation. Read more about it here: https://lnkd.in/gUKEQ2Kp

Excited to share that our paper "Comparing Developer and LLM Biases in Code Evaluation" has been accepted to COLM 2026 and the ICML DL4C Workshop! As LLMs are increasingly deployed as judges to evaluate code, a key question remains: Do they actually care about the same things human developers care about? To find out, we introduced TRACE, a framework designed to evaluate LLM judges in realistic, interactive software engineering settings. Key takeaways from our findings: 📉 Alignment Gap: Even the best LLM judges underperform human annotators by 12–23% when predicting developer preferences. 🔍 Systematic Biases: TRACE exposed significant sources of misalignment. For instance, in code completion settings, LLM judges overemphasize functionality, whereas real developers prioritize code clarity. 🛠️ Code Quality Mismatch: The majority of these misalignments map directly to standard software engineering code quality criteria where models and humans weigh priorities completely differently. Huge thank you to Ryan Shar for his collaboration throughout this project! Also deeply grateful to Valerie Chen and Wayne Chi for their guidance, and my collaborators Zichu Wu and Shyam Agarwal . Check out the full preprint on arXiv if you're interested in LLM evaluation in code settings: https://lnkd.in/gD_FDKW9

honors_and_awards.title: 3rd Place - PioneerHacks IV
honors_and_awards.description: Won third place overall among 109 other participants at the overnight PioneerHacks IV hackathon hosted by Juniper Networks. In a span of 24 hours, we came up with the idea for our project, hoophub, built out the project, and created a presentation for a panel of judges about our product. hoophub is an app that allows users to start impromptu pickup basketball games and notify those nearby, and we built it using Flutter, the Google Maps API, Firebase Auth, and Cloud Firestore.
